text.p: These are the highlights of stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- If positive trends continue in the Macedonian economy, industrial production is expected to increase by 2.5 percent in the first nine months this year. Costs of living in July remained at the June level. Exports in July covered by imports by 70 percent while the trade deficit was $245 million, official statistics say.

- The European Union Commission informed the Macedonian Foreign Ministry that the EU Ministerial Council on budget has recently reached a decision that enables interim use of the Textile Trade Agreement between the EU and Macedonia starting from August 1, 1997.

- The World Bank board is expected to decide in September on approval of a $5 million credit to Macedonia, most of which would be used to rennovate school buildings. Around 300 schools need urgent intervention. The credit has a 10-year grace period and repayment term of 25 years.
- Tourist capacities on Lake Ohrid only 50 percent full with around 15,000 tourists currently holidaying on its shores.

- Opposition VMRO-DPMNE leader Ljupco Georgievski said in interview for daily Nova Makedonija that his party is having problems at local self-government level with other Macedonian opposition Liberal Democratic Party. If such a situation carries on, discussing any coalition at the following parliamentary elections is absurd, Georgievski said.

- Macedonian Interior Ministry announced that the opposition VMRO-DPMNE party is not allowed to celebrate the national holiday Ilinden in Krusevo. VMRO-DPMNE announced it would join the state celebration of this holiday, at which President Kiro Gligorov is expected to deliver a speech.

- Tetovo Municipal Court postpones trial against Tetovo Mayor Alajdin Demiri and Tetovo City Council president Bebi Bedzeti and schedules it for October 14. The court accepted the defence's demand for completing evidence documents.

- In the discussion on electoral laws, the opposition Liberal Democratic Party decided on a purely proportional model. VMRO-DPMNE announces that it will continue exerting pressure for early parliamentary elections from September. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
